(p-197)Surah Al-'Asr (The Time)

Meccan, and its number of verses is three.

﴿By the time﴾. God, glory be to Him, swore by the prayer of 'Asr (ʿaṣr, the afternoon prayer), on account of its outstanding excellence; or by the late afternoon (ʿashiyy), which is the period between the decline of the sun (zawal) and sunset (ghurub), just as He swore by the forenoon (ḍuḥā); or by the era of Prophethood (ʿaṣr al-nubuwwa), because its excellence is manifest over all other eras; or by time (al-dahr), because it encompasses the wondrous events, both those that endure and those that pass away.

Indeed, mankind is in loss. ﴾Indeed, mankind is in loss﴿ meaning: they are in loss in their trade and their pursuits, and in spending their lives on their desires. The definite article in "al-insan" (mankind) is for the genus, and the indefinite "khusr" (loss) is for magnification.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 103, verse 3:

﴿Except for those who have faith and do righteous deeds﴾ — so they are in a commerce that will never fail, for they have sold what is perishable and base and bought what is lasting and precious, and they have exchanged the lasting righteous deeds for the morning and evening (fleeting) things. How excellent is such a transaction, how profitable it is! This is an explanation of their perfecting themselves. And His, exalted be He, saying: ﴿and they enjoin upon one another the truth﴾ ... etc., is an explanation of their perfecting others, i.e., some of them enjoin on others the matter that is established, which cannot be denied, and whose good effects do not cease in either abode, namely, the whole of good: faith in God, mighty and majestic, and following His books and messengers in every belief and action. ﴿And they enjoin upon one another patience﴾, i.e., patience in refraining from sins toward which the soul yearns by the natural disposition of human beings, and patience in performing acts of obedience that are burdensome to perform, or patience in what God, mighty and majestic, tests His servants with. The singling out of this mutual enjoining for mention, although it is included under mutual enjoining to the truth, is to show the complete importance attached to it; or because the first refers to the rank of worship, which is doing what pleases God, exalted be He, and the second refers to the rank of servanthood, which is contentment with what God, exalted be He, has done. For patience does not mean merely restraining the soul from what it craves of action or inaction; rather, it is receiving what comes from Him, exalted be He, with good grace and contentment, outwardly and inwardly. From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Asr, God, exalted be He, will forgive him, and he will be among those who enjoined upon one another the truth and enjoined upon one another patience."
